source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
DartPoints Charleston sits in Ladson, South Carolina, with 1.3 MW of published IT capacity. Among the four South Carolina facilities that have published a megawatt figure on their operator pages, this campus ranks third, and its 1.3 MW represents roughly 20 percent of the 6.6 MW total published across those four sites. The remaining ten of the fourteen mapped facilities in the state publish no capacity figure at all, so the true scale of South Carolina's data center inventory is larger than the numbers show.

At 1.3 MW of IT load, the raw compute headroom is limited. Assuming 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density for mixed enterprise workloads, the campus supports on the order of 130 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a density more typical of AI training configurations, that same 1.3 MW yields roughly 32 racks. Neither figure is an operator claim, and the operator does not publish a rack count or a power density target on the page this site read.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications this site holds for this facility. For an organization evaluating AI infrastructure, 1.3 MW is a modest footprint, more consistent with regional edge or enterprise colocation than with large-scale model training or inference, where campus IT loads typically begin in the tens of megawatts. Whether DartPoints Charleston is positioned for AI workloads specifically is not addressed by the published data.
